cues.en: Health is the most valuable thing we have in life, but we tend to forget that until we lose it.
cues.zh: 健康是我们生命中最宝贵的东西，但我们往往直到失去它才意识到这一点。

cues.en: We're living longer than ever before, which is great. But an unforeseen consequence of this is that we also spend a larger and larger portion of our lives being sick.
cues.zh: 我们的寿命比以往任何时候都长，这很好。但一个意想不到的后果是，我们生命中生病的时间占比也越来越大。

cues.en: Getting old currently means spending more time in pain.
cues.zh: 如今，变老意味着要在痛苦中度过更多时间。

cues.en: So scientists are trying to shift the attention of the medical community from optimizing lifespans
cues.zh: 所以科学家们正试图把医学界的注意力从优化寿命

cues.en: to optimizing
cues.zh: 转向优化

cues.en: healthspans,
cues.zh: 健康寿命，

cues.en: the part of our lives during which we're disease free.
cues.zh: 也就是我们生命中免于疾病的那段时间。

cues.en: To do this, we need to attack the root cause of almost all bodily defects, aging itself.
cues.zh: 要做到这一点，我们需要攻克几乎所有身体缺陷的根源——衰老本身。

cues.en: Unbeknown to most people, the science of aging has made enormous progress in the last few years with human trials about to begin in the near future.
cues.zh: 多数人不知道的是，衰老科学在过去几年取得了巨大进展，人体试验即将在不久后启动。

cues.en: Let's look at three examples of discoveries that might benefit people who are alive right now.
cues.zh: 我们来看三个可能让现在活着的人受益的发现。

cues.en: One, senescent cells.
cues.zh: 第一，衰老细胞。

cues.en: Your cells have an expiration date.
cues.zh: 你的细胞也有“保质期”。

cues.en: Each time one of your cells divides, it copies its chromosomes.
cues.zh: 你的细胞每分裂一次，就会复制自己的染色体。

cues.en: Because of the way this works, they lose a tiny bit of DNA at the ends.
cues.zh: 由于这种机制，它们会在末端丢失一小段 DNA。

cues.en: This could be catastrophic,
cues.zh: 这可能会是灾难性的，

cues.en: so to protect themselves, we have long segments of DNA called telomeres that sort of act like the stiff bits at the end of shoelaces,
cues.zh: 所以为了保护自己，我们体内有很长的 DNA 片段，叫作端粒，有点像鞋带末端的硬头，

cues.en: but they shrink with every cell division.
cues.zh: 但它们会随着每次细胞分裂而缩短。

cues.en: In some cells, after a number of divisions, the telomeres are gone, and the cell becomes a zombie,
cues.zh: 有些细胞经过多次分裂后，端粒消失了，细胞就变成僵尸，

cues.en: a senescent cell.
cues.zh: 也就是衰老细胞。

cues.en: Senescent cells stay around and don't die.
cues.zh: 衰老细胞会留在体内，不会死亡。

cues.en: The older you get, the more of them there are inside you.
cues.zh: 你年纪越大，体内这类细胞就越多。

cues.en: They harm tissue around them and are linked to many diseases that accompany old age, like diabetes and kidney failure.
cues.zh: 它们会伤害周围的组织，并与许多伴随衰老而来的疾病有关，比如糖尿病和肾衰竭。

cues.en: But what if you could kill them off?
cues.zh: 但如果你能把它们清除掉呢？

cues.en: Scientists genetically engineered mice so that they could destroy their senescent cells as they pleased.
cues.zh: 科学家对小鼠进行了基因改造，使它们可以随心所欲地摧毁自己的衰老细胞。

cues.en: Older mice without senescent cells were more active. Their hearts and kidneys worked better, and they were less prone to cancer.
cues.zh: 没有衰老细胞的老年小鼠更活跃。它们的心脏和肾脏功能更好，也更不容易患癌症。

cues.en: Overall, they lived up to 30% longer and in better health than average mice.
cues.zh: 总体而言，它们比普通小鼠多活了多达30%，健康状况也更好。

cues.en: Since we can't genetically engineer all of the cells in the human body, we need to find another way to get rid of our senescent cells.
cues.zh: 既然我们无法对人体所有细胞进行基因改造，就得另想办法清除衰老细胞。

cues.en: But how do we kill them without harming healthy cells?
cues.zh: 但怎样才能杀死它们，又不伤害健康细胞呢？

cues.en: Most cells in the body commit a programmed cell suicide when they're damaged,
cues.zh: 体内大多数细胞在受损时会启动程序性的细胞自杀，

cues.en: but senescent cells don't.
cues.zh: 但衰老细胞不会。

cues.en: It turns out that they under produce a protein that tells them when it's time to die.
cues.zh: 原来，它们某种蛋白分泌不足，而这种蛋白正是告诉它们何时该死亡的信号。

cues.en: So in a late twenty sixteen study, mice were given an injection of this protein.
cues.zh: 所以在2016年末的一项研究中，小鼠被注射了这种蛋白质。

cues.en: It killed eighty percent of all their senescent cells while causing almost no harm to healthy cells.
cues.zh: 它杀死了它们体内80%的衰老细胞，同时对健康细胞几乎无害。

cues.en: The treated mice became generally healthier and even regrew lost hair.
cues.zh: 接受治疗的小鼠整体变得更健康，甚至重新长出了失去的毛发。

cues.en: As a result, there are a number of new companies looking at treatments involving senescent cells, and the first human trials will start soon.
cues.zh: 因此，已有多家新公司在研究涉及衰老细胞的疗法，首批人体试验也即将开始。

cues.en: Two,
cues.zh: 第二，

cues.en: NAD plus.
cues.zh: NAD+。

cues.en: Cells are made from hundreds of millions of parts. They're the structures,
cues.zh: 细胞由数亿个部件构成。这些部件是结构，

cues.en: machines,
cues.zh: 机器，

cues.en: messages,
cues.zh: 信号，

cues.en: and the catalysts that make reactions happen.
cues.zh: 以及让反应得以发生的催化剂。

cues.en: All these parts constantly need to be destroyed, cleaned up, and rebuilt.
cues.zh: 所有这些部件都需要不断被销毁、清理和重建。

cues.en: As we age, this process becomes less effective, and so parts become crumpled, bunched up, or are removed slower.
cues.zh: 随着年龄增长，这个过程效率会下降，于是部件变得皱缩、堆积，或者被清除得更慢。

cues.en: Or they are no longer produced in the quantities we need.
cues.zh: 或者不再以我们所需的数量产生。

cues.en: One of these parts is NAD plus a coenzyme that tells our cells to look after themselves.
cues.zh: 其中一种部件就是 NAD+，一种辅酶，它告诉我们的细胞要照顾好自己。

cues.en: At age 50, we only have about half as much in our bodies as we do at age 20.
cues.zh: 50岁时，我们体内的这种物质只有20岁时的一半左右。

cues.en: Low amounts of it are linked to a whole bunch of diseases, from skin cancer to Alzheimer's,
cues.zh: 它含量低与一大堆疾病有关，从皮肤癌到阿尔茨海默病，

cues.en: cardiovascular
cues.zh: 心血管

cues.en: disease,
cues.zh: 疾病，

cues.en: and multiple sclerosis.
cues.zh: 以及多发性硬化症。

cues.en: But NAD plus can't enter cells, so we can't get it as a pill.
cues.zh: 但NAD+无法进入细胞，所以没法做成药丸来补充。

cues.en: But scientists noticed that other more flexible substances could enter cells and would then turn into NAD plus in sight.
cues.zh: 但科学家注意到，其他更灵活的物质可以进入细胞，然后在细胞内转化为NAD+。

cues.en: multiple trials on mice showed that they boosted the modification of skin, brain, and muscle stem cells.
cues.zh: 多项小鼠试验显示，它们促进了皮肤、脑和肌肉干细胞的修复。

cues.en: They were rejuvenated,
cues.zh: 它们恢复了活力，

cues.en: had a higher ability to repair their DNA, and had a slightly increased lifespan.
cues.zh: DNA 修复能力更强，寿命也略有延长。

cues.en: This even got NASA interested, which is looking for a way to minimize the DNA damage astronauts would be exposed to from cosmic radiation on Mars missions.
cues.zh: 这甚至引起了 NASA 的兴趣，NASA 正在寻找办法，尽量减少宇航员在火星任务中因宇宙辐射而受到的 DNA 损伤。

cues.en: There are human trials being planned right now, but it's too soon to say if this will boost our health span or even lifespan.
cues.zh: 目前正在筹划人体试验，但要说这能否延长我们的健康寿命甚至总寿命，还为时过早。

cues.en: But NAD plus is a serious candidate and could become the first human antiaging pill.
cues.zh: 但 NAD+ 是一个强有力的候选者，可能成为第一款人类抗衰老药丸。

cues.en: Three,
cues.zh: 第三，

cues.en: stem cells.
cues.zh: 干细胞。

cues.en: Stem cells are like cell blueprints that sit at various places in the body and copy themselves to produce a steady flow of fresh young cells.
cues.zh: 干细胞就像细胞蓝图，分布在身体各处，通过自我复制持续产生新鲜年轻的细胞。

cues.en: But they decline as we age, and so we decline too.
cues.zh: 但它们会随年龄增长而衰退，我们也就跟着衰退。

cues.en: Without new parts, human bodies break.
cues.zh: 没有新部件，人体就会损坏。

cues.en: In mice, scientists observed that as the stem cells in their brains disappeared,
cues.zh: 在小鼠中，科学家观察到，随着它们大脑中的干细胞消失，

cues.en: they started to develop diseases.
cues.zh: 它们开始出现疾病。

cues.en: So they took stem cells from baby mice brains and injected them directly into the brains of middle aged mice.
cues.zh: 于是他们从幼鼠大脑中取出干细胞，直接注射到中年小鼠的大脑中。

cues.en: More specifically, the hypothalamus,
cues.zh: 更具体地说，下丘脑，

cues.en: a part that's involved in regulating a lot of bodily functions.
cues.zh: 它是参与调节许多身体功能的部位。

cues.en: The fresh stem cells reinvigorated
cues.zh: 新鲜的干细胞重新焕发了

cues.en: older brain cells by secreting micro RNAs that regulated their metabolism.
cues.zh: 较老脑细胞的活力：干细胞分泌的微小RNA调节了这些脑细胞的代谢。

cues.en: After four months, brain and muscles worked better than those of untreated mice, and on average, they lived 10% longer.
cues.zh: 四个月后，它们的大脑和肌肉比未治疗的小鼠运作得更好，平均寿命还延长了10%。

cues.en: Another study took stem cells from mice embryos and injected them directly into the hearts of older mice.
cues.zh: 另一项研究从小鼠胚胎中提取干细胞，直接注射到老年小鼠的心脏中。

cues.en: As a consequence, they had improved heart function, could exercise 20% longer, and weirdly enough, their hair regrew faster.
cues.zh: 结果，他们的心脏功能改善了，运动时间能延长20%，而且奇怪的是，头发长得更快了。

cues.en: What all of this tells us is that there is not a single magic bullet with which to cure aging.
cues.zh: 这一切告诉我们，治愈衰老并不存在单一的灵丹妙药。

cues.en: It requires a complex array of different therapies.
cues.zh: 这需要一套复杂多样的不同疗法。

cues.en: We can kill off senescent cells to clear away the junk, give ourselves fresh new stem cells to fill the gap, all while regulating the metabolism of the other cells using medication.
cues.zh: 我们可以杀死衰老细胞来清除垃圾，补充新鲜干细胞来填补空缺，同时用药物调节其他细胞的代谢。

cues.en: This video comes with a big caveat.
cues.zh: 这个视频有一个重要前提。

cues.en: After all, these studies have been carried out on mice.
cues.zh: 毕竟，这些研究都是在老鼠身上进行的。

cues.en: There's no guarantee the same therapies would work in us to the same extent, but they are proof of concepts.
cues.zh: 不能保证同样的疗法在我们身上也能达到同样效果，但它们属于概念验证。

cues.en: To learn more about how we can modify our own health span, we need human trials.
cues.zh: 要更多了解如何改善我们自己的健康寿命，我们需要人体试验。

cues.en: We've only covered a tiny part of the research that's being done right now and only scratched the surface of these ideas.
cues.zh: 我们只涵盖了当前研究的一小部分，也只触及了这些想法的表面。

cues.en: The field of health span extension needs more attention and funding.
cues.zh: 延长健康寿命这一领域需要更多关注和资金。

cues.en: If it gets it, all of us might enjoy growing old without pain.
cues.zh: 如果它能成功，我们所有人或许都能无痛地老去。

cues.en: If you now want to support the research on aging directly, you can do so at lifespan.io,
cues.zh: 如果你现在想直接支持衰老研究，可以访问 lifespan.io，

cues.en: a community of people actively supporting the scientists working to cure aging.
cues.zh: 这是一个积极支持致力于治愈衰老的科学家们的社群。

cues.en: Check them out to learn about the latest advances and visit their blog or group on Facebook.
cues.zh: 去看看他们，了解最新进展，并访问他们的博客或 Facebook 群组。

cues.en: The lifespan team also kindly supported the creation of this video with a donation and their expertise.
cues.zh: lifespan 团队还慷慨地通过捐款和专业知识支持了本视频的制作。

cues.en: If you want to help us make more of our videos, you can do so on patreon.com.
cues.zh: 如果你想帮助我们制作更多视频，可以在 patreon.com 上支持我们。
